title: Individual growth variability in farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar L.): the role of social interactions
study_system_detail: farmed Atlantic salmon under semi-commercial/commercial-style rearing conditions
study_objective: To investigate the development and persistence of individual growth variation in farmed Atlantic salmon and the roles of behaviour, social interactions, competition and intrinsic competitive ability.
temporal_scope: multiple linked studies over several months
focal_factor_detail: social interactions, dominance, feeding competition and social status
comparison_detail: fish of different size/growth trajectories; higher versus lower feeding competition; presence versus absence of larger fish; good versus poor performers
study_outcome_detail: individual growth trajectories, growth rate, size variation and recovery of non-growing fish
evidence_passage: The thesis contains linked studies using semi-commercial tank conditions, behavioural observations, biochemical reconstruction of social status and comparisons of fish differing in size, growth trajectory and competitive/social status.

title: Seasonality in live fish movements and its effects on epidemic dynamics
study_system_detail: Scottish salmon farm movement network spanning freshwater and seawater production phases
study_objective: To quantify how seasonal patterns and ordering of live fish movements between Scottish salmon farms affect the course of simulated epidemics.
facility_detail: farm network; freshwater and seawater farms
focal_factor_detail: live fish movements and seasonality as transmission pathways
comparison_detail: observed-order network A versus randomized-order network B versus simulated network C; seasonal versus non-seasonal versions; freshwater versus seawater farms
study_outcome_detail: epidemic size, prevalence and time-to-peak under alternative movement-network structures and transmission parameters
evidence_passage: The full thesis chapter corresponding to the paper describes three network structures: observed movement network A, randomized-order network B and simulated network C, with stochastic SIR epidemic simulations used to test effects of seasonality and movement order.
